title: Nerello Mascalese
description: Etna's red grape: pale, perfumed and firm, grown high on the slopes of an active volcano.
L: Describe Nerello Mascalese's flavours and structure

Nerello Mascalese gives pale ruby wines with red cherry, raspberry, wild herbs, flowers, smoke and a mineral, volcanic edge. Tannins are firm and fine, acidity high. It's often compared to Pinot Noir for its paleness and perfume, and to Nebbiolo for its tannin and structure.

Nerello Mascalese is named after the Mascali plain, below Mount Etna, in eastern Sicily. DNA suggests it's a cross of Sangiovese and Mantonico Bianco. It ripens late, often in October, which suits Etna's altitude: cool nights and long autumns preserve acidity and aroma.
Which grapes is Nerello Mascalese often compared with?
It shares Pinot's paleness and perfume and Nebbiolo's tannin.

Look for pale ruby colour, red fruit, herbs and a smoky, stony edge, with firm, fine tannins and fresh acidity. It's paler than most southern reds and more structured than you'd guess from its colour.
Nerello Mascalese is deeply coloured and low in acidity.
Not true. It's pale and has high acidity.
Nerello Mascalese is pale, perfumed and firm
It's named after the Mascali plain below Etna
It's compared with Pinot Noir and Nebbiolo

Nerello Mascalese grows mainly on the slopes of Mount Etna, Europe's highest active volcano, at 400 to over 1,000 m. Most vineyards are on the north side, around villages like Passopisciaro, Randazzo and Solicchiata. Smaller amounts grow elsewhere in north-east Sicily, like Faro near Messina.

Altitude cools Etna's vineyards: nights can be 15 to 20 degrees cooler than days, keeping acidity and aroma. Etna receives more rain than the rest of Sicily, and harvest can run into late October. It's one of the few places in southern Italy with an almost Alpine climate.
Match each term to Nerello Mascalese.
Nerello Mascalese belongs to north-east Sicily.

Etna Rosso DOC must be at least 80% Nerello Mascalese. The rest can be Nerello Cappuccio, which adds colour and softness. Old Etna vineyards are often field blends, with white grapes mixed in. Carricante is Etna's main white grape.
Nerello Cappuccio can make up the rest.
Nerello Mascalese grows mainly on Etna's north slope
Altitude gives cool nights and late harvests
Etna Rosso is at least 80% Nerello Mascalese

Etna's soils are made of volcanic sand, ash and lava, of different ages. They're poor, well-drained and rich in minerals. Each lava flow created different soils, so neighbouring vineyards can taste different. Phylloxera struggles in volcanic sand, so many old vines are ungrafted, trained as alberello, bush vines, on terraces.

Etna's vineyards are divided into contrade, local districts, often defined by lava flows. In 2011, Etna DOC recognised 133 contrade, which can appear on labels, like Burgundy's crus. Producers like Frank Cornelissen, Andrea Franchetti of Passopisciaro and Marc de Grazia drove Etna's revival from the early 2000s.
Why are many Etna vines ungrafted?
Sandy volcanic soils protect against phylloxera, so many old vines survive on their own roots.
Look for a contrada name on an Etna label, such as Rampante or Feudo di Mezzo. Like a Burgundy cru, it tells you exactly where the grapes grew.
Contrade are local districts, often defined by lava flows.
Etna's volcanic soils vary with each lava flow
Many old vines are ungrafted bush vines on terraces

Etna Rosso's freshness and fine tannin suit a wide range: grilled tuna and swordfish, pasta with tomato and aubergine, roast pork, lamb with herbs and mushrooms. Its acidity handles tomato; its moderate weight doesn't overwhelm fish.

Serve at 15 to 17 degrees. Simple Etna Rosso is good within five years; contrada wines from old vines can age 10 to 20 years, gaining earth and dried flowers. A short decant helps young, tannic examples.
Why can Etna Rosso pair with grilled tuna?
Its moderate weight and fine tannin don't overwhelm the fish
Lighter body and fine tannin suit meaty fish.
Try an Etna Rosso with pasta alla Norma, Sicily's aubergine, tomato and ricotta salata pasta. The wine's freshness meets the tomato.
Contrada wines from Etna can age 10 to 20 years.
Yes. Their acidity and tannin let them develop.
Etna Rosso suits tuna, tomato pasta and mushrooms
Contrada wines can age 10 to 20 years
Where does Nerello Mascalese mainly grow?
On Etna's slopes, especially the north side.
Etna Rosso must be at least ____% Nerello Mascalese.
At least 80%, with Nerello Cappuccio allowed.
Nerello Mascalese is pale, perfumed and firm
It grows high on Etna's volcanic slopes
It's a fresh, versatile food wine
